The theft-attempt detection method uses a combination of acceleration from IMU and authentication from BLE proximity. This developed product can provide location accuracy of 10 meters with 98.1% certainty and an average theft-detection response time of 2.71 seconds.

title: Implementation of Progressive Web App-Based Applications for Vehicle Tracking Systems.
abstract: The user has to be able to see the information from the server with ease, so the device's information sent from the server has to be easily accessed by the user. The application has to be made so that users across all platforms can easily access the application. Developing an application that can be accessed on all platforms can make the time to make the app a lot less consuming. Nowadays, web application development has supported web pages with capabilities close to natively developed applications. Progressive Web App, commonly known as PWA, allows for the integration of web-based applications with native applications. PWA is a web application that can enable native applications, especially in developing multi-platform applications that can be accessed by various platforms. In this project, the PWA application was developed in the form of a vehicle-based supporting device that can monitor car location from Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices and prevent an attempt to steal the vehicle. Two interfaces will be made in this project for the car's owner and the police. The car owner can access the car location, and the police can also access it when the car owner makes a report. The police interface is made so that it can track the stolen car with a legal approach. The car owner can access the web application and then change the desired device mode so that when there is a theft indication car owner can report it to the police, and the police can investigate it. The result of this implementation is that the user, who is a car owner and police, can both access the location visualization in the interface, and the interface can be accessed on all platforms.

title: Design and Implementation of Drowsiness Detection System Based on Standard Deviation of Lateral Position.
abstract: Drowsiness can decrease concentration while driving. The decreased concentration while driving makes a slower response in making decisions about road conditions. Roads with monotonous characteristics and low traffic density can also reduce driver alertness. This condition can lead to traffic accidents. However, drivers sometimes do not realize that they are sleepy. Therefore, a system is needed to detect drowsiness and provide warnings to drivers. To overcome that problem, we propose a system for detecting and alerting a driver's sleepiness based on the deviation from the lane. This system is designed using the Python programming language and the OpenCV library. Based on the results of experiments that we have done, the calculation of the Standard Deviation of the Lateral Position accuracy reaches 96.54% during the day and 91.08% at night.

title: Scholarship Recipients Prediction Model using k-Nearest Neighbor Algorithm and Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique.
abstract: This research aims to develop a prediction model for scholarship recipients using the k-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) and Synthetic Minority Over Sampling Technique (SMOTE) algorithms. The method in model development uses the Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM) which consists of phases of business understanding, data understanding, data processing, modeling, evaluation, and deployment. The dataset used is the Indonesian Smart College Card (KIP-K) Scholarship data in the real world obtained at one of the universities in Indonesia. The evaluation of the model uses a confusion matrix to calculate the values of accuracy, recall, precision, F1-Score, and AUC. The research results show seven attributes that influence the selection process for prospective scholarship recipients, namely non-academic achievement scores, selection test scores, survey scores, interview scores, economic condition scores, academic achievement, and choice of study programs. While the results of model testing produce the best model performance at a value of k=3 with 90.12% accuracy, 85.57% precision, 96.51% recall, 90.71% F1-score, and 0.957 AUC, which are included in the Excellent Classification category. Based on the test results, the model can be applied to a prediction system for prospective scholarship recipients at higher education institutions to make it more targeted.

title: Improving Radar-Camera Fusion-based 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Vehicles.
abstract: Object detection is essential for autonomous driving as it provides knowledge of the state of the surrounding objects. Aside from the objects' 3D bounding boxes, 3D object detection also estimates the objects' velocity and attribute. Radar-camera fusion-based object detection methods have the potential to deliver accurate and robust results even in harsh conditions while being more affordable than lidar-based solutions. However, current radar-camera fusion-based methods are still significantly outperformed by their lidar-based counterparts, even when radar has access to direct velocity measurement which lidar lacks. In this work, we propose a feature-level radar-camera fusion-based object detection architecture. Our architecture associates preliminary detections produced by an image-based pipeline with radar detection clusters using a frustum-based association mechanism. By using radar detection clusters instead of individual points, we can extract features that allow the model to use the geometry of the clusters to refine the preliminary detections. We evaluated our architecture on the nuScenes dataset and achieved a nuScenes detection score (NDS) of 0.465. We also find that our architecture achieved significantly better objects' orientation, velocity, and attribute estimation results compared to other radar-camera fusion-based methods.

title: Panoptic Segmentation Datasets for Rail-based Autonomous Vehicle Under Mixed-traffic Scenario.
abstract: The challenge of percept the complex environment through visual recognition has turned the tide of research on image recognition toward panoptic segmentation by unifying the distinct task of instance and semantic segmentation into a single architecture. This work applies panoptic segmentation for the inner-city tram in the environment where the railway intersects with the road. Our study on Cityscapes, COCO-Stuff, and RailSem19 public datasets has limitations due to unsuitable semantic and instance masks for our mixed traffic scenario. Thus, we consider creating our self-curated dataset, which was collected on the route of the Batara Kresna railbus, for the model to generalize our local context better. The data consists of a combination of 1000 frames of images with a dense-pixel panoptic annotation. Among those sets, 200 of them are specified and taken using the front camera to maximize the occurrence of the railway. We decided to calculate the occurrence of an object and class distribution as an initial data quality assessment.

title: Predicting Price Movement of the BTCUSDT Pair Using LightGBM Classification Modeling for Cryptocurrency Trading.
abstract: This research proposes a machine learning-based system that aims to form an investment strategy that is capable of buying and selling cryptocurrencies. Predicting the price movement of crypto assets has a number of challenges, especially due to the high volatility of trading prices. Traditionally this process is carried out by conducting technical analysis using technical indicators which requires extensive knowledge and experience to get maximum profit in cryptocurrency trading. The CRISP-DM methodology was applied to create a classification model to predict the movement of the BTCUSDT cryptocurrency pair using a tree-based classification algorithm with the Gradient Boosting framework, namely the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM). The Logistic Regression algorithm was used as a comparison. As input data, the klines dataset of the BTCUSDT cryptocurrency pair is used and feature engineering is carried out in the form of labelling (up/down) as well as a number of technical indicators commonly used in trading activities. The prediction results of the classification model are then used in the further evaluation stage by being tested (used for trading) against the original data of BTCUSDT price movements for one month and the Return on Investment (ROI) obtained is evaluated against the Buy and Hold strategy. Based on the evaluation results, the resulting model has a better performance than Logistic Regression, but the model's performance has not been able to exceed the ROI value of the Buy and Hold strategy consistently and still can't generate profit.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning to Automate Cryptocurrency Trading.
abstract: This research produces a deep reinforcement learning model for algorithmic trading of cryptocurrencies. The model aims to help traders earn greater profits than using traditional strategies. Although traditional strategies can generate profits, they require considerable knowledge, experience, and time to generate optimal profits. Models are trained to trade on the cryptocurrency market. Model inputs are 1 minute interval candlestick data and technical indicators for the BTC/USDT cryptocurrency pair. The model produces an output in the form of a buy, hold, or sell signal. Models are created with the PPO algorithm and a custom environment that follows the gym interface. The performance of the model is compared to the Buy and Hold strategy. The tests that have been carried out show that the model produced in this study still cannot beat the Buy and Hold strategy.

title: Rainfall Nowcasting based on Satellite Images using Convolutional Long-Short Term Memory.
abstract: Rain that falls at a small and moderate rate is a blessing but incessant rainfall can bring many adverse effects such as loss of life, and destruction of property, crops and fields. One of the ways that can reduce the negative effects of natural disasters like this is to study trends and make predictions about what will happen. The predictive system, e.g. a nowcasting model can play an important role in dealing with rain issues, especially being able to provide early warning before bad weather occurs and this to some extent can help save lives and property. However, the determination of predictive models is a technically challenging task because rainfall is a non-linear phenomenon. In this research, a combination of a deep learning model called Convolutional Long-Short Term Memory (ConvLSTM) assisted by digital image processing is applied to real-time radar time series and satellite images. The goal is to predict the next event in a sequence of images with different timestamps i.e., 10-minutes, 30-minutes, and 60-minutes. Experimental results were evaluated with performance metrics using the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM).

title: Evaluation of Fuzzy PID controller design for coffee roasting temperature regulation.
abstract: The time-temperature progression is one of the most influential factors in determining the beverage's overall quality. This is because the roasted bean takes on noticeably different qualities in the cup depending on the roasting profile used, even though both varieties will have the same colour at the end of the process. This is specifically due to the fact that roasted beans take on the characteristics of the roasting profile used. Thus, the temperature profile of the coffee bean pile while it is being roasted can be replicated in a significant manner by employing a readily available PID controller. Due to the difficulty of adjusting the PID parameters, however, the controller's performance is seldom optimized. This article compares the performance of PID controllers tuned with M-constrained Integral Gain Optimization (AMIGO) to that of two Fuzzy-PID controllers with three and five membership functions. The step responses, setpoint tracking, and disturbance rejection simulation test results for the Fuzzy-PID controller indicated a significant performance improvement. This includes an average improvement of greater than 90 % in overshoot and greater than 10 % in settling time.

title: Hybrid Feature Selection with K-Nearest Neighbors for Optimal Heart Failure Detection.
abstract: The selection of an optimal feature subset plays an important role in medical data handling. The accuracy of diagnosis is affected by the data dimensionality and is often degraded caused of irrelevant information in the features. Filter-based feature selection can be applied to select the most significant features based on ranking. However, the use of an independent filter-based technique is still incapable to identify the optimal features as it does not consider the top dominant feature subsets among feature selectors. Therefore, a hybrid filter-based feature selection is proposed in this study by considering the emergence rate of the selected features identified in Information Gain (IG), Correlation (CR), Chi-Squared (CS), and Relief-F (RL). An advantage of the hybrid filter-based technique is that the emergence of the selected features in each filter can be considered to determine the optimal feature subsets. The proposed technique is examined using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifier with 10-fold Cross-validation on the heart failure clinical record dataset retrieved from the UCI Machine Learning repository. We apply the proposed technique to predict the patients' survival and to rank the most significant features. The results indicate that the proposed technique successfully improves the classification performances for heart failure detection with an accuracy of 84.61%, a precision of 0.84, recall of 0.84, and an F1-score of 0.84. It has been observed that the fewer selected features in the feature subset, the more optimal the classification performance.

title: Template-Based Supervised Deep Homography Estimation Based on SqueezeNet.
abstract: Homography estimation is a common method used to solve many computer vision problems. Homography can be used to implement measurement on instruments based on image processing, replacing the common sensor required for a direct approach with the measured objects. Using the deep neural network in estimating homography is already quite popular among researchers and computer vision-related developers. Many networks are being implemented to solve homography based on classification network to find the transformation matrix. However, implementation of homography from previous studies with complex network requires high computing and is difficult to apply to embedded systems with limited capacity. Our research demonstrates the deep homography estimation for image transformation calibration based on template image with simpler network and requires less computational capability. We use the renowned SqueezeNet network model for the main network backbone with modification on the network head to solve the corner displacement of the homograph. We create the dataset from template image of symbols and train the network from the beginning. We change the output of the SqueezeNet classifier to regression output to acquire the displacement of the corner of perturbed image. To validate the network results, we compare the perturbed input image with the result of homography matrix prediction against the main template image to get the confidence level of the predicted homographic image. The results of our study are close to those of similar studies using more complex networks, but our network requires significantly less computing and power consumption and shorter training time.

title: Linear Quadratic Gaussian using Kalman Network and Reinforcement Learning for Discrete-Time System.
abstract: A problem arises when implementing the control scheme into a system, the limitation of the number of sensors used causes not all state information from the plant can be obtained. In addition, the data measurement process also often contains noise. Therefore, implementing the optimal control scheme directly becomes difficult. The status estimation method proposed in this study utilizes the use of an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) as a function approximation. On the other hand, the development of optimal control implementation has also experienced a fairly massive increase. Some of the existing optimal control solutions can only be carried out offline and depend on the dynamics' model of the system to be controlled. The combination of KalmanNet and the Value Iteration (VI) algorithm is used to adapt the role of the Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) method in designing control procedures to produce high performance. Tests were carried out on a cart-pole system in a discrete-time domain. The use of the combination of these methods could make the closed loop system towards a value of 0 and the evolution of the estimator gain is smoother, namely with the norm of 2.33S4E-04.

title: Online Learning Facial Expression Detection using Simplified AlexNet Deep Learning Architecture: Image Data Samples Comparison Experiment.
abstract: Online learning is one of the methods for students to interact with their teachers. However, interactivity aspects in online education should be evaluated. The method to automate the detection of students' enthusiasm when participating in online learning is still not much found. In this paper, we define the facial expressions that could show when students participate in online learning: bored, confused, and excited/delighted. We built a classifier system for these online learning face expressions. We collected a small dataset (for around 480 images) containing face images with these three facial expressions to be trained for the deep learning model. We proposed simplified AlexNet architecture as a deep learning model for a relatively small dataset, that is, AlexNet architecture with lower parameters (such as filters and the number of neurons in the fully connected layer). Image preprocessing methods such as resizing and augmentation are applied for the experiment. We also compare the model performance, given a distinct (three kinds) number of training data (480 samples, 1,500 samples, and 3,000 samples). When our proposed model is trained with these three kinds of training samples amount, the model performance consecutively has an average accuracy of 78.69%, 84.53%, and 90.80% in 5-Fold Cross Validation. Using ANOVA Test, we get a p-value of 0.00073, which is statistically significant to reject the null hypothesis that training samples do not affect our proposed model's accuracy.

title: IoT Device Control with Offline Automatic Speech Recognition on Edge Device.
abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) on edge device still barely used in industry. Most of ASR such as speech-to-text commonly depend on the network presence. This is the disadvantages of using the server-based architecture that cannot always be reliable and available. In some conditions, the speech recognition need to be used in offline condition and edge-processing. Raspberry Pi, one of many edge devices will use offline ASR platform with only runs on python language. These platforms will encourage to do speech recognition in offline condition and edge device processing. Vosk, Picovoice/Cheetah, Sopare runs with python language and some of it required Word-Error-Rate (WER) on the result to validate result value. The 5 simple commands trained on each platform. Overall result, these 3 platforms are working well in offline environment with good accuracy (>80%). Vosk has around 84% accuracy, Picovoice/Cheetah has around 72% and Sopare has around 95% accuracy. Picovoice/Cheetah need an internet connection at first application startup.

title: Design and Development of a Daily Recording System for Vocational High School Field Work Practice Participants.
abstract: Online Prakerin is a program implemented by the Information and Communication Technology Research Center of the Bandung Institute of Technology since 2021 which allows Vocational High Schools throughout Indonesia to register their students to carry out field work practices online. Monitoring and Evaluation is one form of activity that must be carried out in running an online internship program with the aim that field work practice participants can benefit from the online internship program. In 2021 there will be 90 SMKs and 4,198 students enrolled in the online prakerin program. Monitoring and evaluating 4198 students require enormous energy and effort. Seeing these conditions, the researcher proposes the design and development of an Android-based application with the aim of making it easier for online internship participants to report daily activities so that the daily activities of online internship program participants can be monitored and can later be evaluated as consideration for providing value results from online internships. The stages carried out in this study are as follows: The first stage is the analysis of system requirements at this stage the authors identify problems by conducting interviews with the Information and Communication Technology Research Center, Bandung Institute of Technology. The two stages of system design at this stage the authors design the requirements that have been obtained in the first stage and describe them in the form of use case diagrams. The three stages of making the system at this stage the researchers carried out the implementation of making the system from the use case diagram that had been made in the second stage. The result of the third stage is an android-based application that can be used by students to report daily activities and a website-based application that can be used by the Information and Communication Technology Research Center of the Bandung Institute of Technology to monitor the activities of online internship participants. The fourth system testing at this stage the authors conducted a system test by giving questionnaires to students and to the Information and Communication Technology Research Center, Bandung Institute of Technology.

title: Gamification of Animal Recognition Learning for Children with Deaf in Elementary School Using Dance Pad Media.
abstract: Madrasah Ibtiyah Muhammadiyah Special Program (MIM PK) Kartasura is an elementary school for children with special needs, one of which is the deaf, located in Kartasura. As technology develops, the MIM PK school continues to strive to improve innovation and quality in learning, one of which is using educational games. Based on the age of elementary school children, education is needed in recognizing the things around them, one of which is the introduction of animals so that they will know about the various kinds of animals that are around them. The solution that the researcher provides is using animal recognition gamification for children with special needs (ABK) with hearing impairment in 4th grade using the Media Dance Pad. The method used is divided into several stages including requirements analysis, system design, implementation and code writing, testing, evaluation, and maintenance. The making of this educational game uses Construct 2 as the software used in making the game and uses a dance pad as a connecting device for the controller and Figma as a component in the game. Based on the BlackBox and questionnaire tests that have been carried out, it is hope that the educational game is useful and easily as a learning media that makes it easier for students to receive the material, especially in animal recognition.

title: Design and Analysis of IoT-based Aquarium Monitoring System for Guppy Fish Habitats.
abstract: Total lifespan of guppies in the wild varies and it is typically identified as around 2 years. Variations characteristics of life guppies are observed in different populations, indicating that different evolutionary pressures exist. Guppy eats a variety of foods including brine shrimp, bloodworms, or pellet. Too many foods in the water tank or aquarium will cause pollution and affect guppies' life habitats and most probably they get poisoned and died. This research aims to design and analyze an IoT-based monitoring system for Guppy fish in suitable habitats. An Arduino Uno acted as the microcontroller and temperature sensor, turbidity sensor, and pH sensor were installed as inputs. PuTTY software was used to record the data from all the sensors and synchronized daily to google drive. Four experiments have been conducted to identify suitable foods for the guppies. The result presents the analysis of Baby Brine Shrimp (BBS) type of fish food is safe due to the changes in pH value for the experiments are less than pellet type pH value. The turbidity level shown in experiment 3 is also very promising as it is the lowest turbidity level with 3.1 NTU. It is identified that a good range for guppy habitat is from 22°C to 32°C. This research is significant for guppies' fish breeders in monitoring and maintaining the quality of good guppies' habitats in agriculture.

title: 6th International Conference on Software and e-Business, ICSEB 2022, Shenzhen, China, December 9-11, 2022.
Proceedings of the 4th International Conference on Software Engineering and Development, ICSED 2022, Xiamen, China, November 25-27, 2022.
abstract: The intensification of population aging has brought pressure on public medical care. In order to reduce this pressure, we combined the image classification method with computer vision and used audio data that is easy to collect in nursing homes. Based on MelGAN, transfer learning, and Vision Transformer, we propose an application called Risevi (A Disease Risk Prediction Model Based on Vision Transformer), a disease risk prediction model for nursing homes. We first design a sample generation method based on MelGAN, then refer to the Mel frequency cepstral coefficient and the Wav2vec2 model to design the sample feature extraction method, perform floating-point operations on the tensor of the extracted features, and then convert it into a waveform. We then design a sample feature classification method based on transfer learning and Vision Transformer. Finally, we obtain the Risevi model. In this paper, we use public datasets and subject data as sample data. The experimental results show that the Risevi model has achieved an accuracy rate of 98.5%, a precision rate of 96.38%, a recall rate of 98.17%, and an F1 score of 97.15%. The experimental results show that the Risevi model can provide practical support for reducing public medical pressure.

title: 12th International Conference on System Engineering and Technology, ICSET 2022, Bandung, Indonesia, October 3-4, 2022
abstract: In many countries, water quality monitoring is limited due to the high cost of logistics and professional equipment such as multiparametric probes. However, low-cost sensors integrated with the Internet of Things can enable real-time environmental monitoring networks, providing valuable water quality information to the public. To facilitate the widespread adoption of these sensors, it is crucial to identify which sensors can accurately measure key water quality parameters, their manufacturers, and their reliability in different environments. Although there is an increasing body of work utilizing low-cost water quality sensors, many questions remain unanswered. To address this issue, a systematic literature review was conducted to determine which low-cost sensors are being used for remote water quality monitoring. The results show that there are three primary vendors for the sensors used in the selected papers. Most sensors range in price from US$6.9 to US$169.00 but can cost up to US$500.00. While many papers suggest that low-cost sensors are suitable for water quality monitoring, few compare low-cost sensors to reference devices. Therefore, further research is necessary to determine the reliability and accuracy of low-cost sensors compared to professional devices.
